description: Screening of image files for hidden payloads (metadata text, Unicode smuggling, bytes appended after the image data), served through the image-forensics /v1/screen API. The expected endpoints are POST /v1/screen and GET /readyz; suppliers MAY expose more but consumers MUST NOT depend on it. No model is involved: answers are deterministic for a given rule table, identified by pipeline_fingerprint. The pixels are never examined, so a clean verdict says nothing about text painted into the image.

rpc_types.backend_hint: image-forensics service on :8000 (image-forensics-service, endpoints.screen enabled); mount at /
rpc_types.notes: Only POST /v1/screen and GET /readyz are expected. Request body is multipart/form-data with exactly one of media (file) or media_base64; url sources are off by default and MUST NOT be relied on. Send the original file bytes: the container is the evidence.

serving.backend: Any server exposing POST /v1/screen and GET /readyz with the request/response shape of the OpenAPI document in specs[1]. Recommended: image-forensics-service with endpoints.screen enabled. No model, GPU, sibling service or network access is required.
serving.notes: A screening-only deployment needs no detector section and downloads nothing; it can run on a small CPU host. Keep image URL fetching disabled. It is recommended to front it with the HA RelayMiner. See the docs in specs[0] for the full runbook.
